description.en-US: Find, install and update open-source Android apps straight from their source.Lumen Store looks at the apps already installed on your phone, finds the ones that are open source, and keeps them up to date by downloading releases directly from F-Droid, IzzyOnDroid, GitHub, GitLab and Codeberg. No account is required, and nothing is installed behind your back.It also works as a discovery tool: browse GitHub projects, read their READMEs and screenshots, follow developers, and install what you like in one tap. Features Scan and update - Scans your installed apps and matches them against the F-Droid and IzzyOnDroid indexes and GitHub releases - Shows which apps have updates and installs them in one tap - Picks the right APK for your device ABI - Background scanning with notifications for new updates - Full rescan and index redownload when you need a clean slate Explore - Browse and search GitHub repositories - Rich README rendering with tables, badges, SVG images and screenshots - GitHub user and organization profiles with repositories, activity and stats - Search Google Play listings and jump to their open-source counterparts - Anti-feature warnings for apps from F-Droid indexes Sources - Built-in F-Droid and IzzyOnDroid repositories - Add your own repositories from GitHub, GitLab or Codeberg - Optional GitHub token for a higher API rate limit, with no sign-in required to use the app - DNS over HTTPS support for more reliable connections Personalisation - Material 3 design with dynamic seed colors and multiple themes - Light and dark modes - Custom app icon shapes - Animated live backgrounds: aurora, bubbles, stars, ripples and fireflies - English and Persian (فارسی) with full RTL support Backup and sharing - Backup and restore your app list, with optional automatic backups - Share apps with lumenstore://app/ deep links - Opens Google Play, F-Droid and GitHub links directly in the app Download Grab the latest APK from the Releases page.

Android app that inspects device signals: key attestation, TEE, kernel and environment probes. It reports signals only. It is not a Play Integrity verdict and does not prove a device is unmodified. Requirements

- JDK 17 - Android SDK with platform 36 - Gradle 8.14+ (or generate the wrapper with gradle wrapper --gradle-version 8.14.3) Build

gradle :app:assembleDebug gradle :app:testDebugUnitTest gradle :app:assembleRelease

The release build is signed with a keystore generated on first build (app/release.keystore and app/keystore.properties). Both are git-ignored. Keep them private and back them up if you distribute releases, since updates must be signed with the same key. Languages

English and Persian. License

summary.en-US: A customized combination of Termux terminal and Debian terminal.

description.en-US:
Terbian is an open-source Debian terminal environment for Android, inspired by Termux and built with Java. It brings the power of Linux to your Android device through PRoot, without requiring root access.

Designed for developers, Linux enthusiasts, and power users, Terbian combines a modern Material 3 interface with persistent terminal sessions, customizable themes, and a portable Debian environment.

- Debian on Android — Run Debian 12 in a PRoot environment without root access. - Local Shell — Access the native Android shell alongside Debian sessions. - Multi-Tab Terminal — Manage multiple terminal sessions in one interface. - Session Management — Long-press tabs to close the current session, other sessions, or all sessions. - Material 3 UI — A modern Android interface with customizable terminal themes. - Custom Themes — Black, Burnt Espresso, Gruvbox, Solarized Dark, Dracula, Nord, and Light Paper. - Extra Keys Row — Quick access to essential terminal keys. - Persistent Sessions — A foreground service helps keep terminal sessions alive while using other apps. - Adaptive Launcher Icon — Includes a monochrome icon layer for supported Android launchers.

Java · Android · Linux · Debian · Gradle · Material 3

Build the debug APK using Gradle:

./gradlew assembleDebug

Fast · Secure · Customizable DNS Changer for Android

- Protocols: UDP · TCP · DoT (853) · DoH (443) - Catalog: Gaming DNS pairs + Cloudflare, Google, Quad9, AdGuard, Vanilla - Custom servers: manual entry or import from clipboard - Modern UI: new layout with floating navigation and a redesigned icon - Themes: 14 Material themes (11 dark, 3 light) - Live ping per server, real-time DNS logs - Root mode: optional DNS change without VPN - Auto-reconnect on network change - Languages: فارسی / English Protocols

Android 7.0 (API 24)+ · Target SDK 34 · VPN permission (or root) Build

bash git clone https://github.com/deepcodecreate/Dc-Dns-Changer.git cd Dc-Dns-Changer ./gradlew assembleDebug

Share your phone's VPN connection with other devices over the hotspot. The app runs a local HTTP and SOCKS5 proxy and includes a full network monitor. Features

- HTTP proxy and SOCKS5 proxy with a foreground service - Home screen with live shared traffic and the devices using the proxy - Network monitor - Overview: internet status, DNS time, public IP, active network, phone and proxy traffic - Wi-Fi: signal, link speed, band, channel, security, IP configuration, hotspot - VPN: interface, protocol, addresses, routes, exit IP and country - Devices: local network scan and proxy clients - Ping: live ping, jitter, loss, history chart, multi-target comparison - Logs: filterable event log with share and clear - 8 themes in light and dark, wallpaper colors, pure black, icon shapes, font size, motion levels - Persian and English Usage

1. Turn on your VPN and the phone hotspot. 2. Open the app and tap Start proxy. 3. On the other device, join the hotspot and set the proxy to the address shown on the Home screen. Build

The app has no native code, so one APK runs on arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86 and x8664. The build also writes a universal APK and one APK per ABI.

Requirements: JDK 17 and Gradle 8.0 or newer.

gradle assembleDebug gradle assembleRelease
